children: DataMeds AI reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $2.7 million, up 50% sequentially, and net income of $10.5 million. Gross profit was $431,880, while the company recorded an operating loss of $3.4 million. Diluted earnings per share were $2.72.
Revenue was $2.669 million, compared with $3.013 million in the third quarter of 2025.
Gross profit was $431,880, versus $231,012 a year earlier.
Operating loss was $3.374 million, compared with an operating loss of $31.548 million in the prior-year quarter.

Net income was $10.536 million, compared with a net loss of $34.318 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company attributed the improvement largely to gains from extinguishment of debt and liabilities, along with lower expenses.
Diluted earnings per share were $2.72, compared with a diluted loss per share of $23.07 a year earlier.
Corexa Pharmacy dispensing drove the sequential revenue increase, according to the company.

DataMeds AI launched the Health Lives Here mobile app with the NFL Alumni Health marketing platform to connect customers with Corexa Pharmacy for FDA-approved GLP-1 medications and Forzet medical food.
In October, the company obtained an exclusive license to the REBOOT GLP-1 patient-management platform and related intellectual property, which it says will support AI-assisted patient engagement.

Corexa Pharmacy launched compounded peptides under the FDA’s enforcement-discretion policy. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved and have not been evaluated by the FDA for safety or efficacy. The company also signed a non-binding MOU with a Florida HMO to deploy the app to more than 25,000 members.

Following its acquisition of Helomics, a cancer diagnostics laboratory, the company cited Humana South Carolina Medicaid coverage for the ChemoFx assay and plans to expand the laboratory’s testing services. DataMeds AI also said it regained full compliance with Nasdaq listing standards.
